I’ve spent enough time working alongside a Los Angeles–based social media marketing agency to see how the operation actually runs, and it raised serious concerns. The pitch is polished and heavy on buzzwords, but in practice the strategy often feels thin and designed to justify large retainers rather than deliver proportional results.

“Proof” of success frequently relies on clients who already had momentum before the agency came on board, which looks more like taking credit than creating growth. Reporting tends to highlight surface-level metrics instead of clear, measurable outcomes.

My takeaway is simple: do not buy the pitch. Ask for specific, verifiable case studies that demonstrate real growth over time. Real marketing is measurable, and real results do not need a smokescreen.
